svg.title: CBC mode bit-flipping attack mechanics
svg.desc: Legitimate CBC decryption recovers plaintext block two by XORing the decryption of ciphertext block two with the previous ciphertext block one, yielding the expected string admin=0;user=alice. An attacker who flips one byte in ciphertext block one changes the corresponding byte of plaintext block two predictably, forging admin=1;user=alice and escalating privilege, while plaintext block one decrypts to unusable random garbage. The stated mitigation is an AEAD mode such as AES-GCM, whose authentication tag rejects the modified ciphertext.
svg.text: Flipping a ciphertext bit C1[i] alters plaintext P2[i] predictably while scrambling P1 into random garbage
• Decrypting block 2 XORs previous ciphertext block C1 to recover plaintext P2
• Authenticated user role parsed normally by application handler
Flip bit in C1: C1' = C1 ⊕ ('0' ⊕ '1')
• Attacker modifies 1 byte in C1 to target specific character in P2
• Side Effect: P1 decrypts into random unusable garbage data
• Target bit flipped to '1'! Privilege escalation achieved
• Mitigation: Use AEAD (AES-GCM) with Auth Tags to reject modified C1
